<<<FROZEN GEMINI QUESTION-ONLY VISUAL ADDENDUM>>>
NH2OH converts COF-8 to COF-9 without changing the alternating 3-connected honeycomb topology. In COF-8, each D2-derived black node contains a 1,3,5-triazine and three para-phenylene arms, while each red E1-derived node is a 1,3,5-substituted benzene connected through three -CH=C(CN)- segments. In COF-9, each pendant cyano group at those same linker positions is replaced by the drawn amidoxime group -C(=N-OH)-NH2. Six amidoxime groups are shown around the perimeter of a hexagonal pore.

The repeat boundary is indicated by four separated blue dashed cuts across outward connectors; the marks do not form a rhombus and are not centered on four triazines. The inset photograph shows a bright blue fluorescent cuvette on the left and a clear/nonfluorescent cuvette on the right, joined by a rightward arrow labeled + UO2^2+. The response page has blanks for q_e in mg g^-1 and for the ratio COF-9 : UO2^2+.
<<<END FROZEN GEMINI QUESTION-ONLY VISUAL ADDENDUM>>>

Cardiolipins are a family of acyclic phospholipids differing in fatty acid residues. They are essential for
energy production and membrane stability. Defects can lead to certain diseases. PL1 belongs to this
family. Using only the structural elements a-d in the quantities stated below, it is possible to assemble
the non-ionised form of PL1. R is a hydrocarbon substituent in the fatty acid structure.




PL1 does not contain any peroxide bonds.

Some cardiolipins are chiral molecules, even if they contain four identical fatty acid residues, as in the case
of PL1. One enantiomer of PL1 is found in prokaryotes and eukaryotes, and the other only in archaea. All
other diastereomers of PL1 are achiral molecules, since they have a plane of symmetry. Do not consider
the chirality of phosphorus atoms as stereocentres.
PL1 is a diprotic acid with the same acidic groups. Its second deprotonation is less favourable
(𝑝𝐾𝑎2 ≫ 𝑝𝐾𝑎1 ) due to the special, stable structure of monoanion Y.

T5. Cardiolipins

In this problem you are asked to be creative and build molecules from fragments. For instance, if you
are required to draw a chiral phospholipid such as W using fragments a-e, it can be assembled as shown
below.




Cardiolipins are a family of acyclic phospholipids differing in fatty acid residues. They are essential for
energy production and membrane stability. Defects can lead to certain diseases. PL1 belongs to this
family. Using only the structural elements a-d in the quantities stated below, it is possible to assemble
the non-ionised form of PL1. R is a hydrocarbon substituent in the fatty acid structure.




PL1 does not contain any peroxide bonds.

     5.1     Tick one correct statement regarding the value of n (number of type a frag-             1.0 pt
             ments).
             (a) n is an even number,
             (b) n is an odd number,
             (c) n can be either an odd or an even number.

Some cardiolipins are chiral molecules, even if they contain four identical fatty acid residues, as in the case
of PL1. One enantiomer of PL1 is found in prokaryotes and eukaryotes, and the other only in archaea. All
other diastereomers of PL1 are achiral molecules, since they have a plane of symmetry. Do not consider
the chirality of phosphorus atoms as stereocentres.
PL1 is a diprotic acid with the same acidic groups. Its second deprotonation is less favourable
(𝑝𝐾𝑎2 ≫ 𝑝𝐾𝑎1 ) due to the special, stable structure of monoanion Y.

[p.3 red] SOLUTION:
[p.3 red] To obtain the diastereomer of PL1 with a plane of symmetry, we must construct
[p.3 red] a symmetric structure from the given fragments. Glycerol backbones can only
[p.3 red] be linked through phosphate groups since there is no peroxide bond present.
[p.3 red] The number of glycerol moieties suggests that one glycerol occupies the central
[p.3 red] position with the remaining fragments arranged around it to achieve an overall
[p.3 red] plane of symmetry. The number of a fragments in PL1 is n = 3·3 – 2·2 – 4 = 1.
[p.3 red] So, PL1 has 𝑑2𝑐−𝑏−𝑐(𝑎) −𝑏−𝑐𝑑2 skeleton. Two options, presented below, can
[p.3 red] have a plane of symmetry:
[p.3 red] The PL0 structure is achiral, so it cannot be PL1. All possible stereoisomers of
[p.3 red] PL1 are as follows:
[p.3 red] SOLUTION:
[p.3 red] Enantiomer 2 is found in prokaryotes and eukaryotes. These organisms use
[p.3 red] glycerol 3-phosphate for cardiolipin synthesis, while archaea use glycerol 1-
[p.3 red] phosphate for this purposes and synthesise enantiomer 1:
[p.3 red] SOLUTION:
[p.4 red] PL1
[p.4 blue] For drawing of enantiomer 1 or 2 as PL1: 4 points.
[p.4 blue] For drawing the correct structure of PL1 with wrong or missing stereochemistry: 3 points.
[p.4 blue] For drawing achiral PL0 structure: 2 points.
[p.4 blue] Any other structure that uses exactly 1×a, 2×b, 3×c, 4×d and contains no peroxide bond: 1 point.
[p.4 red] Intramolecular hydrogen bond between the phosphoric acid residue and the alcohol group signifi-
[p.4 red] cantly reduces the 𝑝𝐾𝑎2 value.
[p.4 blue] For any correct tautomer of Y: 2 points.
[p.4 blue] For a tautomer of Y (not shown above) with a hydrogen bond between the two phosphate groups:
[p.4 blue] 1 point
[p.4 blue] Correctly drawn structures with incorrect PL1 structure are also accepted.
[p.4 blue] For structures containing hydrogen bond between phosphoric acid residues and esters 0 point, be-
[p.4 blue] cause they are possible for each phosphoric acid residue even in molecular form and don’t make
[p.4 blue] difference between 𝑝𝐾𝑎1 and 𝑝𝐾𝑎2.

(𝑝𝐾𝑎2 ≫ 𝑝𝐾𝑎1 ) due to the special, stable structure of monoanion Y.

Four lipid phase structures are illustrated, each composed of lipid molecules represented by a circular head group attached to squiggly tails:
- (a) micellar: A circular cross-section of a spherical assembly where the head groups form the outer surface and the tails point inward toward the center.
- (b) lamellar: A planar bilayer assembly consisting of two parallel layers of lipids. The tails of the two layers point toward each other, while the head groups face outward on the top and bottom surfaces.
- (c) hexagonal: An array of cylindrical assemblies. In each cylinder, the head groups form the outer surface and the tails point inward toward the central axis.
- (d) inverse hexagonal: An array of cylindrical assemblies. In each cylinder, the tails point outward and the head groups point inward toward the central axis.

[p.9 red] SOLUTION:
[p.9 red] The hydrolysis of PL1 proceeds through breaking of 8 ester bonds, which re-
[p.9 red] quires 8 water molecules. So, PL2 also contains all these ester bonds and has
[p.9 red] the same skeleton with PL1 and the residue of molecule Z needs to be located
[p.9 red] in the centre of PL2 due to its symmetry:
[p.9 red] In the case of Z reducing the number of covalent bonds, leads to decreasing
[p.9 red] numbers of C, H or O atoms:
[p.9 red] - removing each C atom decreases the number of covalent bonds by 3;
[p.9 red] - removing a pair of H atoms forms a C=C or C=O double bond, which reacts
[p.9 red] with 𝐻2 in presence of catalyst;
[p.9 red] - removing each O atom decreases the number of covalent bonds by 1.
[p.9 red] Thus, Z is propane-1,3-diol: it contains only C, H, and O; does not react with
[p.9 red] H2 in the presence of a catalyst; has one fewer covalent bond; and is more
[p.9 red] symmetrical than glycerol.
[p.9 red] Note that replacing OH with H makes the PL2 molecule more symmetrical – a
[p.9 red] 𝐶2 rotation axis appears:
[p.9 red] This diastereomer of these enantiomers isn’t chiral due to its symmetry plane.
[p.9 red] PL3 needs to be synthesised from the same precursors and via the same
[p.9 red] metabolic pathways as PL1. So, it can be one of the following enantiomers:
[p.9 red] SOLUTION:
[p.10 red] The right structure is typical of prokaryotes and eukaryotes, while the left one is possible for archaea.
[p.10 red] PL3 demonstrates the structure of phosphatidic acid derivatives such as phosphatidylcholine.

The AFM sequence starts from decachloroanthracene. It loses 2 Cl radicals to A; A loses 5 to B, B loses 2 to C, and C loses 1 to C14. A also has a branch losing 3 Cl radicals to D. The provided A is an anthracene framework with eight remaining Cl substituents; the two radical dots are at the lower carbon of the central ring and the upper carbon of the right-hand outer ring. The upper carbon of the central ring remains Cl-substituted.

The synthesis starts from 4-(4-bromophenyl)-4-hydroxycyclohexa-2,5-dien-1-one. Step 1 NaH; step 2 uses 4-lithio-4'-(OTBS)biphenyl to give F. F +2 equiv TESCl/imidazole -> G; G +LiOH -> H (C36H47BrO3Si2); H +PhI(OAc)2/H2O -> I. I then undergoes NaH and p-bromophenyllithium -> J; J +2 equiv TESCl -> K; K +2 equiv Ni(COD)2/2,2'-bipyridine -> L (C54H80O4Si4); L +4 equiv TBAF then excess SnCl2 -> [5]CPP. TBS is tert-butyldimethylsilyl, TES triethylsilyl, COD cycloocta-1,5-diene. Answer boxes F-L are completely blank and do not seed product connectivity.

A chemical reaction scheme is provided for the synthesis of [5]CPP, detailing the formation of intermediates **F** through **L**. 

**Reaction Sequence:**
*   **Starting Material to F:** The starting material is a cyclohexa-2,5-dien-1-one ring. The C4 position (para to the carbonyl) is bonded to an -OH group and a *p*-bromophenyl group (a benzene ring with a bromine atom para to the attachment point). It reacts with "1. NaH" and "2." a biphenyl molecule substituted with a lithium atom ('Li') at one para position and an 'OTBS' group at the other para position, to yield intermediate **F**.
*   **F to G:** **F** reacts with "TESCl (2 equiv.)" over "Imidazole" to yield intermediate **G**.
*   **G to H:** **G** reacts with "LiOH" to yield intermediate **H**. The chemical formula for **H** is provided as C$_{36}$H$_{47}$BrO$_{3}$Si$_{2}$.
*   **H to I:** **H** reacts with "PhI(OAc)$_2$" over "H$_2$O" to yield intermediate **I**.
*   **I to J:** **I** reacts with "1. NaH" and "2." a benzene ring substituted with a lithium atom ('Li') and a bromine atom ('Br') at para positions, to yield intermediate **J**.
*   **J to K:** **J** reacts with "TESCl (2 equiv.)" over "Imidazole" to yield intermediate **K**.
*   **K to L:** **K** reacts with "Ni(COD)$_2$ (2 equiv.)" over "2,2'-Bipyridine (2 equiv.)" to yield intermediate **L**. The chemical formula for **L** is provided as C$_{54}$H$_{80}$O$_{4}$Si$_{4}$.
*   **L to [5]CPP:** **L** reacts with "1. $n$-Bu$_4$NF (4 equiv.)" and "2. SnCl$_2$ (excess)" to yield the final product **[5]CPP**. The structure of **[5]CPP** is shown as a closed cyclic loop of five benzene rings, each connected to its two neighbors at the para positions.

**Legend and Abbreviations:**
*   **COD** = Structure shown as an 8-membered carbon ring with two double bonds separated by two single bonds (cycloocta-1,5-diene).
*   **TBSCl** = Structure shown as a silicon atom bonded to a chlorine atom, two methyl groups, and a *tert*-butyl group.
*   **TESCl** = Structure shown as a silicon atom bonded to a chlorine atom and three ethyl groups.
*   **Imidazole** = Structure shown as a 5-membered aromatic ring containing one -NH- group and one -N= atom.
*   **2,2'-Bipyridine** = Structure shown as two pyridine rings connected by a single bond at their 2-positions.
*   A text note states: "(equiv. = Equivalent, excess = Excess)".

Text at the top of the image states: "Next generation nanobelts were constructed from porphyrin rings and triple bonds using the template synthesis method. *Hint:* **M** is the thermodynamic product and has four types of protons."
Text at the bottom states: "(equiv. = Equivalent)".

**Linear Reaction Scheme:**
A reaction sequence shows the synthesis of intermediate **R** from toluene (methylbenzene):
*   Toluene reacts with "$t$-BuCl (2 equiv.)" over "AlCl$_3$" to yield intermediate **M**.
*   **M** reacts with "1) NBS, (BzO)$_2$", "2) HMTA", and "3) HCl, H$_2$O" to yield intermediate **N**.
*   **N** reacts with "1)" a dipyrromethane molecule (structure shown as two pyrrole rings connected by a single methylene vertex at their 2-positions) and "CF$_3$COOH", "2) DDQ", and "3) Zn(OAc)$_2$" to yield intermediate **O**.
*   **O** reacts with "NBS" to yield intermediate **Q**.
*   **Q** reacts with "1) Pd$^0$, PPh$_3$, CuI", "(C$_6$H$_{13}$)$_3$Si-C$\equiv$CH" (shown as a trihexylsilyl group bonded to a terminal carbon-carbon triple bond), and "2) $n$-Bu$_4$NF" to yield intermediate **R**.

**Legend and Abbreviations:**
Chemical structures for the abbreviations are provided:
*   **HMTA**: Hexamethylenetetramine, shown as an adamantane-like cage with four nitrogen atoms at the bridgeheads and six methylene groups forming the bridges.
*   **DDQ**: 2,3-dichloro-5,6-dicyano-1,4-benzoquinone, shown as a 1,4-benzoquinone ring with two adjacent chlorine substituents and two adjacent cyano (-CN) substituents.
*   **NBS**: N-bromosuccinimide, shown as a 5-membered succinimide ring with a bromine atom attached to the nitrogen.
*   **(BzO)$_2$**: Benzoyl peroxide, shown as two benzoyl groups (phenyl-C(=O)-) connected by a peroxide (-O-O-) bond.

**Template Synthesis Scheme:**
A second reaction scheme shows the template-directed synthesis of nanobelt **P6**:
*   A large template molecule is shown: a central benzene ring fully substituted with six identical branches. Each branch consists of a *para*-phenylene ring bonded to the 4-position of a pyridine ring.
*   An arrow points from the template molecule to a large complex, with reagents "PdCl$_2$, PPh$_3$, CuI" above the arrow. A vertical line from intermediate **R** points down to this arrow, indicating **R** is also a reactant in this step.
*   The resulting large complex consists of the central template molecule whose six pyridine nitrogens are each coordinated (indicated by dashed lines) to the central zinc (Zn) atom of a porphyrin unit. There are six porphyrin units in total, forming a ring around the template. Each porphyrin unit has an 'Ar' group at two opposite *meso* positions. The other two opposite *meso* positions of each porphyrin are connected to the adjacent porphyrin units via butadiyne (-C$\equiv$C-C$\equiv$C-) linkages, forming a continuous closed macrocyclic belt.
*   An arrow points from this large complex to the final product **P6**. Above the arrow is the structure of 1,4-diazabicyclo[2.2.2]octane (DABCO), shown as a bicyclic molecule with two bridgehead nitrogen atoms connected by three -CH$_2$-CH$_2$- bridges.
*   The product **P6** is shown as a repeating unit enclosed in large parentheses with a subscript "6". The repeating unit is a zinc porphyrin with 'Ar' groups at two opposite *meso* positions. The other two opposite *meso* positions are bonded to -C$\equiv$C- groups, with the bonds extending outside the parentheses to indicate they link together to form the cyclic hexamer.

**Answer Booklet:**
The answer booklet provides four empty rectangular boxes labeled **M**, **N**, **O**, and **Q** for drawing the respective structures.

When aromatic rings are joined to form a macrocycle, oxidation or reduction can produce global aro-
maticity, in which π electrons are delocalised around the entire macrocycle. Only the π system forming

is counted only along the bold pathway shown below.

*   **Right Block:** Labeled "**CLR**". An output arrow points right out of this block, labeled "$\text{NH}_3$".
*   **Forward Flow:** An arrow labeled "**M2**" points from the left block to the right block.

**Reference Tables (Equations):**
*   **Progressions: arithmetic geometric:** $a_n = a_1 + d(n - 1)$ ; $a_n = a_1 q^{n-1}$

    *   A schematic representation: A box containing four 'N' atoms connected sequentially in a linear chain by three arcs (N–arc–N–arc–N–arc–N).

**Geometry Options for Catalyst 1 (from A8-2):**
Seven chemical structures are provided as options, arranged in two rows. In all structures, a central 'Fe' atom is coordinated to ligands, and the four 'N' atoms of the tetradentate ligand are connected sequentially by three arcs.
*   **Top row, left:** A 4-coordinate complex with four N atoms. Two N-Fe bonds are wedged, and two are dashed, indicating a tetrahedral geometry.
*   **Top row, second from left:** A 4-coordinate complex with four N atoms arranged in a planar cross around the Fe center, indicating a square planar geometry.
*   **Top row, third from left:** A 5-coordinate complex. One Cl atom is in an axial position (vertical bond). Four N atoms are in equatorial positions (slanted bonds), indicating a square pyramidal geometry.
*   **Top row, right:** A 5-coordinate complex. One Cl atom and one N atom are in axial positions (vertical bonds). Three N atoms are in equatorial positions, indicating a trigonal bipyramidal geometry.

Based on the provided images, the following information is necessary for question 8.4:

**Ligand and Catalyst Information:**
*   The "cartoon structure" for ligand **8** is depicted as a rectangular box containing four 'N' atoms connected sequentially in a linear chain by three arcs (N–arc–N–arc–N–arc–N).
*   Catalyst **1** is synthesized from the reaction of ligand **8** and FeCl₂.

**Catalytic Cycle Mechanism:**
A circular reaction scheme shows the sequential transformation of complexes:
*   **1** converts to **9** with the addition of 2H₂O and loss of 2Cl⁻ (+2H₂O, -2Cl⁻).
*   **9** converts to **10** with the addition of a photon and an electron, and the loss of water (+hν, +1e⁻, -H₂O).
*   **10** converts to **11** with the loss of water and addition of carbon dioxide (-H₂O, +CO₂).
*   **11** converts to **12** with the addition of a photon, an electron, and a proton (+hν, +1e⁻, +H⁺).
*   **12** converts to **13** with the addition of water (+H₂O).
*   **13** converts to **14** with the addition of a proton and loss of water (+H⁺, -H₂O).
*   **14** converts to **15** with the loss of carbon monoxide (-CO).
*   **15** converts back to **9** with the addition of water (+H₂O).

**Answer Booklet Pre-filled Information:**
The answer sheet provides the following partial data for the complexes (where Z = total charge, OS = oxidation state, CN = coordination number, and VE = valence electrons):
*   Complex **11**: OS = +3, CN = 6
*   Complex **12**: CN = 5
*   Complex **13**: OS = +2
*   Complex **15**: VE = 16
*   All other values for Z, OS, CN, and VE for complexes 9-15 are left blank for the student to fill in.
<<<END FROZEN GEMINI QUESTION-ONLY VISUAL ADDENDUM>>>

Based on the provided images, the following information is necessary for question 8.6:

*   **Definitions and Experimental Data:**
    *   Turnover Frequency (TOF) is defined as the number of product molecules formed per active catalyst molecule per hour.
    *   Illumination conditions: LED with wavelength $\lambda = 390 \text{ nm}$ and power = $50 \text{ mW}$.
    *   Catalyst performance: TOF = $8 \text{ h}^{-1}$ for $10 \text{ mg}$ of $\text{C}_3\text{N}_4$ loaded with catalyst **1** at a mass fraction $\omega_{cat} = 3.8\%$.
    *   Molar mass of the catalyst (from the preceding text block): $M_{cat} = 557.21 \text{ g mol}^{-1}$.
*   **Formula Provided:**
    *   Quantum yield, $\varphi = \frac{\text{number of reacted electrons}}{\text{number of incident photons}} \cdot 100\%$
*   **Mechanism Diagram Information:**
    *   The catalytic cycle diagram for the reduction of CO₂ to CO shows two separate steps where an electron is added (each labeled "$+1e^-$") for every one molecule of CO released (labeled "$-CO$").

A reaction coordinate diagram plots the change in Gibbs energy, $\Delta G$ (eV), on the y-axis (scale -0.5 to 2.5) for two competing reaction pathways starting from a common initial state at 0 eV.

*   **Lower pathway (CO production):** From the -0.04 eV state, it proceeds via the following sequential steps: **$+CO_2$** (+0.02 eV), **$+e^-$** (+0.16 eV), **$+H^+$** (-0.36 eV), **$+H^+, -H_2O$** (-0.22 eV), and **$-CO$** (+0.1 eV). *   **Upper pathway (H₂ production):** From the -0.04 eV state, it branches upward via the following sequential steps: **$+H^+$** (+0.756 eV), **$+e^-$** (+1.832 eV), **$+H^+$** (-0.168 eV), and **$-H_2$** (-1.14 eV). The highest energy state reached on this pathway is approximately +2.55 eV relative to the start.

**2. Stacked Bar Chart (from Q8-5):**
A chart shows the mole percentages, $\chi$ (%), of products on the y-axis (scale 0 to 100) for four different conditions labeled **a**, **b**, **c**, and **d** on the x-axis.
*   **Legend:** Blue hatched boxes represent **H₂**; red vertically striped boxes represent **CO**.

*   **Condition b:** A stacked bar showing approximately 28% H₂ (bottom) and 72% CO (top).
*   **Condition c:** A stacked bar showing approximately 8% H₂ (bottom) and 92% CO (top).
*   **Condition d:** A stacked bar showing approximately 4% H₂ (bottom) and 96% CO (top).

**3. Illumination Conditions (from Q8-4 text):**
The four conditions to be mapped are:
*   no irradiation (**N**)
*   irradiation with red light (**R**)
*   irradiation with green light (**G**)
*   irradiation with blue light (**B**)

plexes combined with PS can achieve ~23% quantum yield. In this system, reductive quenching of the
singlet (S1 ) and triplet (T1 ) excited states of a PS by reductant (Red) forms PS•− , which donates electrons
to CO2 through the Mn(I)-containing complex.

<<<FROZEN GEMINI QUESTION-ONLY VISUAL ADDENDUM>>>
The starting cyclic repeat is bracketed with subscript 6 and drawn in a chair with the ring O at upper right and the glycosidic O leaving the rightmost carbon downward. It bears CH2OH upward from the upper-left region, one HO group extending left from the lower-left carbon, and one HO group extending downward/right from the lower-right carbon. Reagents to Y are 1) TBSCl (6 equiv.), pyridine; 2) NaH (12 equiv.); 3) TsCl (6 equiv.). Y is labeled C72H132O24Si6. Reagents from Y are 1) t-Bu4NF; 2) H2O, 100 °C.

In the alpha-cycloaltrin product repeat, the same chair and CH2OH are shown, but both secondary hydroxyl drawings are inverted relative to the starting repeat: the left/lower carbon now has an axial OH bond drawn vertically downward, and the other secondary HO group is drawn above the ring beside the ring oxygen. The product remains bracketed with subscript 6. The page also depicts TBSCl as tert-butyldimethylsilyl chloride and t-Bu as a tert-butyl attachment group; the response page supplies a blank Y chair template.
<<<END FROZEN GEMINI QUESTION-ONLY VISUAL ADDENDUM>>>

This allowed the synthesis of the following $\beta$-CD dimer as a mixture of constitutional linkage isomers."

**Reaction Scheme:**
A starting material reacts to form intermediate **L**, which subsequently reacts to form a $\beta$-CD dimer.
*   **Starting Material:** A schematic representation of $\beta$-cyclodextrin drawn as a large circle containing seven inner rectangular boxes arranged in a ring, and one outer rectangular box attached to the bottom right. The inner boxes are numbered 1 through 7 in red, proceeding counterclockwise.
    *   Box 1 (top left): $\text{CH}_2\text{OH}$
    *   Box 2 (top): $\text{CH}_2\text{OH}$
    *   Box 3 (top right): $\text{HOH}_2\text{C}$
    *   Box 4 (right): $\text{HOH}_2\text{C}$
    *   Box 5 (bottom right): $\text{HOH}_2\text{C}$
    *   Box 6 (bottom left): $\text{CH}_2\text{OH}$
    *   Box 7 (left): $\text{CH}_2\text{OH}$
    *   Outer box: $\text{(OH)}_{14}$
*   **Reaction Arrow 1 (Starting Material to L):**
    *   Above the arrow: 1) NaH (30 equiv.), BnCl (30 equiv.)
    *   Below the arrow: 2) DIBAL-H (2 equiv.)
*   **Intermediate L:** Labeled as **L**.
*   **Reaction Arrow 2 (L to Dimer):**
    *   1) $t$-BuOK, followed by the structure of 5-bromo-1-pentene (an unbranched 5-carbon chain with a double bond at one terminus and a bromine atom at the other).
    *   2) Grubbs I
    *   3) $\text{H}_2$, $\text{PtO}_2$
*   **Product (Dimer):** Two $\beta$-CD schematic circles linked together by an 8-carbon straight alkyl chain. 
    *   **Left circle:** The alkyl chain attaches to the oxygen of a $\text{CH}_2\text{O}-$ group in box 4. Box 1 contains $\text{CH}_2\text{OH}$. Boxes 2, 6, and 7 contain $\text{CH}_2\text{OBn}$. Boxes 3 and 5 contain $\text{BnOH}_2\text{C}$. The outer box contains $\text{OBn}_{14}$.
    *   **Right circle:** The alkyl chain attaches to the oxygen of an $-\text{OH}_2\text{C}$ group in box 4. Boxes 1, 2, 6, and 7 contain $\text{CH}_2\text{OBn}$. Box 3 contains $\text{HOH}_2\text{C}$. Box 5 contains $\text{BnOH}_2\text{C}$. The outer box contains $\text{BnO}_{14}$.

**Provided Chemical Abbreviations:**
*   **DIBAL-H** = Structure shown as an aluminum (Al) atom bonded to one hydrogen atom and two isobutyl groups.
*   **Grubbs I** = Structure shown as a central Ruthenium (Ru) atom double-bonded to a =CH–Ph group, single-bonded to two Cl atoms (one wedged, one dashed), and single-bonded to two $\text{PCy}_3$ groups.
*   **Cy** = Cyclohexyl ring.
*   **Bn** = Benzyl group (a benzene ring attached to a $\text{CH}_2$ group).

**Answer Booklet Template:**
The answer booklet provides a template for drawing compound **L**:
*   A schematic circle identical to the starting material, with seven empty inner rectangular boxes arranged in a ring and one empty outer rectangular box with a subscript "14". The letter **L** is printed in the center of the circle.
